item.title: #2672340: user_user_role_insert should not exist
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 18 files, +276/−53 · yml +182 · php +94/−53
  • Diff: c9e3af7
  • Discussion: #2672340 · 14 contributors · 70 comments
  • Followers: 17
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 14 contributors

Summary

Previously, whenever a user role was created (through the API, a recipe, or during configuration sync), Drupal silently created two extra configuration entities alongside it: a "user_add_role_action" and a "user_remove_role_action", the actions used for bulk-assigning or removing that role from users. This caused a real bug: an install profile or recipe that already exported both the role and its matching action configuration would fail on install with a ConfigDuplicateUUIDException, because the hook tried to create the action a second time. Now, these helper actions are only created when a role is added through the admin "Add role" UI form. Programmatic role creation (custom code, drush, recipes, config sync) no longer creates them automatically. Maintainers of install profiles or recipes that define custom roles need to also export the corresponding system.action.user_add_role_action.* and system.action.user_remove_role_action.* configuration if they want those bulk actions to exist.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: Creating a user_role entity outside of the admin UI role form (via code, drush, config import, or a recipe) no longer automatically creates the paired system.action.user_add_role_action.<rid> and system.action.user_remove_role_action.<rid> config entities.

Technical details

The fix removes the #[Hook('user_role_insert')] implementation (userRoleInsert()) that lived in the user module's hook class and fired on every user_role entity insert, config-synced or not. That logic (skip for the anonymous/authenticated roles, create user_add_role_action.<rid> and user_remove_role_action.<rid> if not already present) is now inlined directly into RoleForm::save(), so it only runs when a role is saved through the admin role-add/edit form. Because the hook no longer runs, standard and demo_umami install profiles and the administrator_role/content_editor_role recipes now ship explicit system.action.user_add_role_action.* and system.action.user_remove_role_action.* YAML config files (e.g. for administrator, author, editor, content_editor roles) instead of relying on the removed hook to generate them at install time. Kernel and functional tests that relied on the old implicit creation (UserActionConfigSchemaTest, BulkFormTest) were updated to create the actions explicitly.

Upgrade

If your install profile, recipe, or custom code creates roles programmatically and you want the bulk "add/remove role" actions to exist, export them explicitly as configuration, following the pattern core now ships, for example:

langcode: en
status: true
dependencies:
  config:
    - user.role.administrator
  module:
    - user
id: user_add_role_action.administrator
label: 'Add the Administrator role to the selected user(s)'
type: user
plugin: user_add_role_action
configuration:
  rid: administrator

Add a matching user_remove_role_action.<rid> file for the remove action. These actions are otherwise only created automatically when a role is created via the admin "Add role" form.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: February 20, 2016
  • Committed: August 17, 2026 (10 years and 2 commits later)

Key contributors

  • alexpott (Chapter Three (acquired by Kanopi Studios))
  • marcingy (Examiner.com)
  • therealssj
  • larowlan (PreviousNext)
  • joegraduate (The University of Arizona)
  • nicxvan (nLightened Development LLC)
  • smustgrave (Mobomo)
  • quietone (PreviousNext)
  • catch (Tag1 Consulting, Inc.)

Collaboration

The change sat dormant for years after alexpott clarified in comment #18 that user_user_role_insert() "is doing something that does not have to happen at all. It's a UI niceness but from an API point-of-view just gets in the way", distinguishing this from a superficially similar issue (#2980237) raised by idebr. When joegraduate revived the patch, smustgrave pushed back on backward-compatibility grounds, arguing the change could silently break contrib tests and install profiles that rely on the automatic action creation, and suggested a formal deprecation path. joegraduate and nicxvan discussed why a conventional deprecation wasn't practical here since the behavior lives inside a hook implementation rather than an invokable API, with nicxvan noting hook implementations aren't strictly covered under Drupal's BC policy. The resolution that shipped was to update core's own install profiles and recipes to export the actions explicitly, so the fix's own change record documents the migration path for anyone else relying on the old implicit behavior.

item.title: #2934063: Remove the workaround in \Drupal\Core\Installer\ExtensionListTrait::setPathname()
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 15 files, +81/−78 · php +81/−78
  • Diff: 566590d
  • Discussion: #2934063 · 7 contributors · 43 comments
  • Followers: 16
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 7 contributors

Summary

Drupal's installer used to carry a special workaround: a static cache and dedicated InstallerModuleExtensionList/InstallerThemeExtensionList classes that remembered extension file paths across the container rebuilds that happen during installation. That workaround is no longer needed because the base extension list classes can now resolve manually seeded pathnames on their own, so the installer-specific machinery has been removed and the classes that implemented it are deprecated. Along the way, a related bug was fixed: when locating a profile's optional config overrides, ConfigInstaller was looking up the profile's directory using the "module" extension type instead of "profile", which is now corrected.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • Deprecation: Drupal\Core\Installer\ExtensionListTrait, InstallerModuleExtensionList and InstallerThemeExtensionList are deprecated in 11.5.0 with no replacement (base extension list classes now provide the same behavior); use Drupal\Core\Extension\ModuleExtensionList / ThemeExtensionList directly. Drupal\Core\Extension\ExtensionList::setPathname() is also deprecated as an internal-only method with no replacement. All are removed in Drupal 13.0.0.

Technical details

install_begin_request(), InstallStorage::getAllFolders() and ExtensionInstallStorage::getAllFolders() no longer prime ExtensionList::setPathname() for the active install profile; they rely on the base ExtensionList's ability to resolve pathnames added via $addedPathNames directly. NormalInstallerServiceProvider no longer swaps the extension.list.module and extension.list.theme service classes to the installer-specific subclasses. ModuleExtensionList::__construct() now writes container-provided pathnames straight into $this->addedPathNames instead of calling the now-deprecated setPathname().

Drupal\Core\Installer\ExtensionListTrait, InstallerModuleExtensionList, and InstallerThemeExtensionList are reduced to backward-compatibility shims that trigger a deprecation notice on use; they are removed in Drupal 13.0.0 with no replacement, since ModuleExtensionList/ThemeExtensionList now cover the same behavior. ExtensionList::setPathname() itself is also deprecated (it remains @internal) with no replacement.

ConfigInstaller::installOptionalConfig() and getProfileStorages() now call $this->extensionPathResolver->getPath('profile', $profile) instead of getPath('module', $profile) to locate the profile's optional config directory, fixing incorrect path resolution for profiles whose directory structure differs from a same-named module.

Upgrade

Code that extends or type-checks against the deprecated classes should switch to the base extension list classes:

// Before
use Drupal\Core\Installer\InstallerModuleExtensionList;
use Drupal\Core\Installer\InstallerThemeExtensionList;

// After
use Drupal\Core\Extension\ModuleExtensionList;
use Drupal\Core\Extension\ThemeExtensionList;

Any code calling \Drupal\Core\Extension\ExtensionList::setPathname() directly should stop doing so; it is deprecated with no replacement and will be removed in Drupal 13.0.0. All three classes and the method continue to work until then but emit E_USER_DEPRECATED notices.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: January 3, 2018
  • Committed: August 16, 2026 (8 years and 2 commits later)

Key contributors

  • dawehner (Chapter Three (acquired by Kanopi Studios))
  • quietone (PreviousNext)
  • andypost (Skilld)
  • catch (Third and Grove)

Collaboration

andypost did the implementation work over an extended period, including debugging a regression in AjaxTest caused by ExtensionPathResolver::getPath() now throwing for unknown extensions during library discovery (split into follow-up #3601471), and splitting the original scope into separate issues for the pathname deprecation (#3601481) and the asset-library fix, at reviewer feedback that the change needed to be split so consumers wouldn't break. catch and longwave reviewed and committed the final, self-contained MR, with catch noting "so much code removed/deprecated."

item.title: #3581816: Move uses of Shortcut from Navigation to Shortcut
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 20 files, +562/−91 · php +555/−81 · yml +7/−10
  • Diff: 7926fc3
  • Discussion: #3581816 · 11 contributors · 54 comments
  • Followers: 14
  • AI disclosures: 1 of 11 contributors

Summary

The Navigation module's "Shortcuts" block used to reach directly into the Shortcut module's render logic, and Shortcut had no awareness of the block it powered in Navigation's layout. This left a gap: if a site uninstalled the Shortcut module while keeping Navigation, the Shortcuts block placement stayed behind in Navigation's block layout configuration, pointing at a module that no longer provided it. This issue moves ownership of the Shortcuts navigation block, its lazy builder, and its layout defaults into the Shortcut module itself, so installing or uninstalling either module now correctly adds or removes the block from Navigation's layout. Existing sites get an update hook that removes any orphaned Shortcuts block left over from before this change.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Config change: New navigation_post_update_remove_shortcut_block() update hook strips any leftover navigation_shortcuts block component from navigation.block_layout config on sites where Navigation is installed but Shortcut is not.

Technical details

The block plugin backing navigation_shortcuts now lives as Drupal\shortcut\Plugin\Block\ShortcutNavigationBlock (marked @internal). Drupal\navigation\Plugin\Block\NavigationShortcutsBlock becomes a thin subclass kept only for backward compatibility, carries @deprecated in drupal:11.5.0 and is removed from drupal:12.0.0, and no longer carries the #[Block] attribute itself, so plugin discovery resolves to the Shortcut class. The lazy builder moved from Drupal\navigation\ShortcutLazyBuilder to Drupal\shortcut\ShortcutNavigationLazyBuilder, and the container registration of the navigation.shortcut_lazy_builder service moved from NavigationServiceProvider to a new Drupal\shortcut\ShortcutServiceProvider, keyed off the navigation.renderer service existing rather than a shortcut-specific one.

Shortcut now implements hook_navigation_defaults() and hook_block_alter() (previously implemented in NavigationHooks) to supply the default block placement and the allow_in_navigation/_block_ui_hidden flags for navigation_shortcuts. Because Navigation stores this plugin placement in simple config (navigation.block_layout), which per #3587499 can't formally express a dependency on Shortcut, shortcut_install() and shortcut_uninstall() now directly add or remove the block component from that config, with a duplicate check for the case where both modules install in the same request. A new navigation_post_update_remove_shortcut_block() post-update cleans up any leftover placement on existing sites. The commit initially shipped with a wrong namespace on the new NavigationUpdateTest fixture test, was reverted, and recommitted with the namespace corrected to Drupal\Tests\navigation\Functional\Update.

Upgrade

Code that instantiates or type-hints Drupal\navigation\Plugin\Block\NavigationShortcutsBlock directly should switch to the new class before Drupal 12.0.0:

// Before (deprecated in 11.5.0, removed in 12.0.0):
use Drupal\navigation\Plugin\Block\NavigationShortcutsBlock;

// After:
use Drupal\shortcut\Plugin\Block\ShortcutNavigationBlock;

Code referencing the internal Drupal\navigation\ShortcutLazyBuilder class directly (not the navigation.shortcut_lazy_builder service, which keeps its name) must update to Drupal\shortcut\ShortcutNavigationLazyBuilder; no deprecation shim was left for this internal class.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: March 27, 2026
  • First commit: August 14, 2026 (4 months later)
  • Last commit: August 16, 2026 (1 day and 4 commits later)

Key contributors

  • quietone (PreviousNext)
  • smustgrave (Mobomo)
  • penyaskito (Acquia)
  • dcam
  • berdir (MD Systems GmbH)
  • alexpott (Acro Commerce)
  • godotislate
  • longwave (Full Fat Things)
  • larowlan (PreviousNext)
  • gábor hojtsy (Acquia)
  • catch (Tag1 Consulting, Inc.)

Collaboration

berdir diagnosed the underlying design problem (comment #16568255): Navigation stores plugin configuration with cross-module dependencies in simple config, which can't formally declare those dependencies, so removing Shortcut broke ConfigImportAllTest. He recommended a quick test exclusion rather than a full refactor, and quietone filed the follow-up #3587499 to track the proper fix. godotislate reviewed the install/uninstall ordering in detail (comments #16602087, #16609667) and found that hook_navigation_defaults already fires on hook_modules_installed, which meant an initially-proposed change to shortcut_install() wasn't actually needed. smustgrave reported using Claude to help add the duplicate-block check that finally made the test suite pass. After the fix first landed, quietone caught that it had to be reverted because of a namespace error in the new update-path test, matching a pattern seen in a similar Olivero test-migration issue, and it was recommitted with the namespace corrected.

Summary

The Settings Tray module (the off-canvas dialog for quickly editing block settings from the front end) is now formally deprecated in Drupal core, following approval in #3576315 to move it to a contributed project. item.title: #3615749: Exclude ckeditor5.css from aggregation
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: main
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 2 files, +4/−4 · php +3/−3 · yml +1/−1
  • Diff: 4e897a5
  • Discussion: #3615749 · 4 contributors · 13 comments
  • Followers: 5
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 4 contributors

Summary

Drupal core no longer includes the large, already-minified ckeditor5.css (about 218KB) in CSS aggregation. Previously, if a site had multiple content types or forms with different CKEditor 5 configurations, this file could be duplicated across several different aggregated CSS files, multiplying the bytes transferred unnecessarily. Excluding it from aggregation means it's served once as its own file and can be cached and reused across pages instead of being bundled repeatedly, cutting the total stylesheet bytes sent to visitors editing content.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The fix sets preprocess: false on the assets/vendor/ckeditor5/ckeditor5.css entry in the ckeditor5 library definition (core.libraries.yml), mirroring the setting already used for ckeditor5.umd.js in the same library. This tells Drupal's asset optimizer to skip this file during CSS aggregation, so it is always delivered as a standalone request rather than concatenated into a page-specific aggregate.

Core's own performance test (doTestNodeAddPagesAuthor) had its expected metrics updated accordingly: StylesheetCount rose from 23 to 27 (the file is now a separate, unaggregated request) while StylesheetBytes dropped from 1,085,546 to 640,654, confirming the reduction in duplicate bytes transferred. This was spun out of #3615654 (adding aggregate_target support to core and ckeditor5 libraries) specifically so the aggregation exclusion could be evaluated and potentially backported on its own.</technical> <parameter name="upgrade">

item.title: #2171395: OptionsWidgetBase should use WidgetInterface::massageFormValues()
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Minor task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 1 file, +35/−17 · php +35/−17
  • Diff: b5abc5d
  • Discussion: #2171395 · 8 contributors · 47 comments
  • Followers: 15
  • AI disclosures: 1 of 8 contributors

Summary

The base class behind Drupal's select, checkboxes/radios, and single on/off checkbox field widgets was refactored to process submitted form values the same way most other field widgets do, through massageFormValues() and extractFormValues(), instead of doing that work inline in its form-element validation callback. This is an internal code-quality cleanup with no intended change in what gets saved: the same values (single or multiple selections, required or optional fields, checkbox/radio or select rendering) are stored as before. It was manually verified by re-testing all these widget combinations and comparing the saved database values against the previous behavior.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

Previously, OptionsWidgetBase::validateElement() (a static #element_validate callback) both validated the required-field constraint and transposed and filtered the raw submitted values, writing the result back with $form_state->setValueForElement(). That bypassed the massageFormValues() hook that WidgetInterface defines and that most other widgets use.

validateElement() now only checks the required constraint. Value processing moved to a new OptionsWidgetBase::extractFormValues() override, which first normalizes single-valued widgets (radios, single select) that submit a scalar into an array via NestedArray::getValue()/$form_state->setValue(), then calls parent::extractFormValues() (from WidgetBase), which in turn invokes the new massageFormValues(). That method filters out the _none placeholder option and unchecked checkbox values (integer 0, which must be excluded with a strict comparison since 0 == 'any string'), then transposes the values from field-keyed to delta-keyed arrays ([$this->column => $value]), matching the format WidgetBase::submit() expects.

massageFormValues() also detects when values are already shaped as delta => [column => value] and returns them filtered but otherwise unchanged. This preserves compatibility with subclasses such as content_moderation's ModerationStateWidget, which overrides validateElement() entirely and calls $form_state->setValueForElement() with values already in that shape rather than relying on the parent's massaging logic.</technical> <parameter name="upgrade">

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: January 11, 2014
  • Committed: August 14, 2026 (12 years and 2 commits later)

Key contributors

  • swentel
  • yched
  • smustgrave (Mobomo)
  • dcam
  • quietone (PreviousNext)
  • catch (Tag1 Consulting, Inc.)

Collaboration

The initial patches from swentel stalled for years because of an edge case yched identified in #comment-8460695: single-valued widgets like radios or a single select can submit a scalar #value rather than an array, so removing the is_array() normalization broke those widgets, as confirmed by failed test runs. The issue was picked up again a decade later by smustgrave, who rewrote the fix using extractFormValues()/massageFormValues(); smustgrave disclosed using Claude Code to help locate extractFormValues() and to identify that unchecked checkboxes submit integer 0, which had to be filtered out to avoid breaking checkbox widget tests. Reviewer dcam raised questions that put the issue into Needs Work, then, once answered, performed manual testing across single and multiple values, required and optional fields, and both the select and checkbox/radio widgets, comparing saved database values against the unmodified code before approving. Committer catch noted the change is a net addition of code rather than a removal, but committed it since other core widgets already implement massageFormValues(), making this consistent with the rest of core.

item.title: #3615308: Use Service Closure in ResourceResponseSubscriber
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: main
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 3 files, +10/−9 · php +10/−9
  • Diff: 7fce698
  • Discussion: #3615308 · 3 contributors · 14 comments
  • Followers: 6
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 3 contributors

Summary

When the rest or jsonapi module is enabled, their ResourceResponseSubscriber event subscribers run on every single HTTP response. Previously each one had the full serializer service injected eagerly, which in turn pulled in every registered normalizer service and all of their own dependencies, even on requests that never produce a REST or JSON:API resource response. That serializer is now wrapped in a service closure and only instantiated the first time it is actually needed to serialize a response body. One reporter measured about 160 fewer classes loaded per request on a site with many normalizers registered. There is no behavior change for REST or JSON:API responses themselves.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: The $serializer constructor parameter of Drupal\rest\EventSubscriber\ResourceResponseSubscriber changed from Symfony\Component\Serializer\SerializerInterface to \Closure; call ($this->serializer)() to obtain the serializer instance. The equivalent @internal Drupal\jsonapi\EventSubscriber\ResourceResponseSubscriber class changed identically.

Technical details

Both Drupal\rest\EventSubscriber\ResourceResponseSubscriber and Drupal\jsonapi\EventSubscriber\ResourceResponseSubscriber now request their serializer service via Symfony's #[AutowireServiceClosure('serializer')] (jsonapi.serializer for the JSON:API variant) instead of #[Autowire(service: ...)], and the constructor property type changed from SerializerInterface to \Closure. The subscribers' onResponse() methods invoke the closure, ($this->serializer)(), only at the point where renderResponseBody() actually needs the serializer, so the serializer (and the chain of normalizer services it aggregates) is only constructed when a resource response is genuinely being serialized rather than on every request the subscriber is invoked for.

Test doubles in ResourceResponseSubscriberTest were updated to pass closures (fn () => $this->prophesize(SerializerInterface::class)->reveal()) instead of the serializer instance directly, matching the new constructor signature.

Upgrade

Code that directly instantiates or subclasses Drupal\rest\EventSubscriber\ResourceResponseSubscriber and passes or reads the $serializer constructor argument must adapt to the new \Closure type:

// Before:
new ResourceResponseSubscriber($serializer, $renderer, $routeMatch);

// After:
new ResourceResponseSubscriber(fn () => $serializer, $renderer, $routeMatch);

Any code reading $this->serializer directly must call it as a closure: ($this->serializer)(). The jsonapi subscriber is @internal and carries no BC guarantee.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: August 6, 2026
  • Committed: August 12, 2026 (5 days later)

Key contributors

  • berdir (MD Systems GmbH)
  • catch (Tag1 Consulting, Inc.)

Collaboration

berdir opened the issue after observing the eager serializer injection on a site with 25 normalizer-related services, and measured (via a preload script generated from dynamic page cache hits) that the closure approach loads about 160 fewer classes per request. berdir then extended the same fix to jsonapi's near-identical subscriber. When smustgrave asked whether a change record was needed, berdir argued no: event subscribers are, like hooks, conventionally excluded from Drupal's BC policy, and no subclasses of either class exist in core. catch, committing the patch, agreed with that BC reasoning for event subscribers, but noted the merge produced unexpected commit conflicts, suggesting some other unbackported constructor change to these classes, and flagged that a separate 11.x backport MR would be needed.

item.title: #3581218: Deprecate .theme file extension
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 12 files, +105/−12 · php +100/−12 · yml +5
  • Diff: e83dee3
  • Discussion: #3581218 · 7 contributors · 75 comments
  • Followers: 15
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 7 contributors

Summary

Drupal has deprecated the practice of putting procedural hook implementations in a theme's .theme file (the old-style magic-autoloaded file, e.g. olivero.theme). Themes are not being deprecated, only that specific file mechanism. Starting in Drupal 11.5.0, if hook discovery finds any function in a .theme file, it triggers a PHP deprecation warning pointing at the change record; this will become a hard removal in Drupal 13.0.0. Theme maintainers should move their remaining procedural hook implementations into OOP hook classes under src/Hook, as most core themes already have.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • Deprecation: Procedural .theme files are deprecated starting in Drupal 11.5.0 (previously targeted 12.0.0) and will be removed in Drupal 13.0.0; hook implementations should move to OOP hook classes in src/Hook.
  • New API: New Drupal\Core\Hook\Attribute\ExtensionFileIsConverted attribute lets a function in a .theme file suppress the deprecation, for legacy multi-version compatibility.

Technical details

The deprecation is emitted from ThemeHookCollectorPass: while collectThemeHookImplementations() walks a theme's files during hook discovery, any file with a .theme extension is recorded in the $deprecatedThemeFiles property; after the container is written, writeToContainer() fires @trigger_error(..., E_USER_DEPRECATED) for each one, with a message naming the file and citing https://www.drupal.org/node/3581222. The message wording was tuned after review from alexpott.

To avoid forcing an all-or-nothing conversion, a new #[ExtensionFileIsConverted] attribute (Drupal\Core\Hook\Attribute\ExtensionFileIsConverted) can be placed on any function inside a .theme file to suppress the deprecation for that file; per its docblock it's meant only for legacy/multi-version support and must not be used once a project's minimum core version is >= 11.3.0. A second commit adjusted the emitted version string from drupal:12.0.0 to drupal:11.5.0 after the team decided to backport the deprecation to the 11.x branch rather than waiting for 12.0.0.

Documentation was also updated to drop stale references to .theme as a valid home for hooks: hook_theme_suggestions_HOOK() and hook_theme_suggestions_HOOK_alter() docs now point to src/Hook with the #[Hook(...)] attribute, and ThemeHandlerInterface::themeExists() / ThemeManagerInterface::invoke() no longer describe theme names as "without the .theme extension".

Upgrade

Convert remaining procedural hooks in a theme's *.theme file into an OOP hook class under src/Hook, tagged with the #[Hook('...')] attribute, matching the pattern already used elsewhere in core.

If a .theme file must be kept temporarily to support older core versions, silence the new deprecation on a per-function basis:

use Drupal\Core\Hook\Attribute\ExtensionFileIsConverted;

#[ExtensionFileIsConverted]
function mytheme_procedural_alter(array &$args): void {
  // ...
}

Note this attribute is only for legacy/back-compat support; once a theme's minimum supported core version is 11.3.0 or later, it must be removed along with the .theme file.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: March 24, 2026
  • First commit: August 2, 2026 (4 months later)
  • Last commit: August 11, 2026 (9 days and 3 commits later)

  • berdir (MD Systems GmbH)
  • catch (Third and Grove)
  • quietone (PreviousNext)
  • alexpott (Acro Commerce)
  • smustgrave (Mobomo)

Code calling options_allowed_values() to fetch a list field's allowed values should switch to the new Drupal\options\OptionsAllowedValuesInterface service. _options_values_in_use() is also deprecated with no public replacement, since its only use was internal to the module's own field-storage-update-forbid check. drupal_static_reset('options_allowed_values') is deprecated too, since allowed values are no longer cached in a static variable. Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • Deprecation: options_allowed_values(), _options_values_in_use(), and drupal_static_reset('options_allowed_values') are deprecated in Drupal 11.5.0 for removal in Drupal 13.0.0.
  • New API: New Drupal\options\OptionsAllowedValuesInterface service (getAllowedValues()) replaces options_allowed_values(), caching results per field via the cache.memory backend instead of a static variable.

Technical details

The original design challenge, visible across years of discussion on this issue, was that options_allowed_values() is called both from field item plugins (which have an entity available) and from the options module's Views filter/argument plugins (ListField, NumberListField, StringListField), which call it without an entity. Earlier patches tried folding the logic directly into ListItemBase::getSettableOptions(), but that didn't work for the Views handlers, so the logic was extracted into a new service instead.

Drupal\options\OptionsAllowedValuesInterface, implemented by Drupal\options\OptionsAllowedValues and registered as an autowired service, exposes getAllowedValues(FieldStorageDefinitionInterface $definition, ?FieldableEntityInterface $entity = NULL): array. It replaces the old drupal_static() cache in options_allowed_values() with per-field entries in the cache.memory backend, keyed by entity type, field name, and whether an entity was passed, and tagged with the field storage's own cache tags plus a new options_allowed_values cache tag so invalidating one field doesn't wipe every field's cached values. ListItemBase::getSettableOptions(), ListItemBase::generateSampleValue(), and the three Views plugins now call this service (the Views plugins receive it via constructor dependency injection, with a deprecated fallback to \Drupal::service() for callers that don't yet pass it).

_options_values_in_use()'s logic moved into a new protected method, Drupal\options\Hook\OptionsHooks::hasValuesInUse(), used only by the module's own field_storage_config_update_forbid hook implementation; no public API replaces it. The hook_field_storage_config_update_forbid() example in options.api.php was updated to query the entity directly with \Drupal::entityQuery() instead of calling the deprecated function.</technical> <parameter name="upgrade">Replace direct calls to the deprecated function:

// After:

  ->getAllowedValues($field_storage_definition, $entity);

  ->condition($field_name . '.value', $values, 'IN')
  ->count()
  ->range(0, 1)
  ->execute();

Summary

Drupal core's test tooling now supports a #[Skip] attribute for marking PHPUnit test methods as skipped, as an alternative to calling $this->markTestSkipped() inside the test body. This makes it obvious from the method's declaration alone that it is skipped, and it takes effect before the test's setUp() runs, so any expensive or Drupal-bootstrapping setup logic is avoided for skipped tests. This is relevant to anyone writing PHPUnit tests against Drupal's test base classes, including contrib module maintainers.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: New Drupal\TestTools\Attribute\Skip PHP attribute to mark a PHPUnit test method as skipped, with an optional message.

Technical details

The new Skip attribute class lives in core/tests/Drupal/TestTools/Attribute/Skip.php, targets methods only (#[\Attribute(\Attribute::TARGET_METHOD)]), and takes an optional $message constructor argument that is passed through to markTestSkipped().

Support for the attribute is wired into Drupal\Tests\DrupalTestCase via a new skipTestWithAttribute() method registered with #[Before(200)], a high priority chosen so it runs before any setUp() logic. It reflects on the current test method for a Skip attribute instance and, if found, calls static::markTestSkipped($attribute->newInstance()->message). Since DrupalTestCase is the common ancestor for Drupal's PHPUnit base classes, the attribute works across unit, kernel, and functional tests. Two existing skips in core were converted as examples: EditorValidationTest::testLabelValidation (no message) and SettingsTest::testRealDeprecatedSettings (with a message), both replacing an inline markTestSkipped() call with #[Skip(...)] on the method.

A follow-up commit (f7eadfbe) also removed the skip from testRealDeprecatedSettings on the 11.x branch after #24 and #25 established it should no longer be skipped there, since the underlying setting deprecation issues (#3591513, #3613344) had landed.

// Before:
public function testSomething(): void {
  $this->markTestSkipped('Reason here.');
  // ...
}

// After:
use Drupal\TestTools\Attribute\Skip;

#[Skip('Reason here.')]
public function testSomething(): void {
  // ...
}

The message argument is optional; #[Skip] alone is valid.

item.title: #3587565: Static cache entities that aren't loaded
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 3 files, +130/−11 · php +130/−11
  • Diff: 2ab239c

Summary

Entity storage previously had no memory of failed load attempts within a request: if code tried to load an entity ID that doesn't exist (a common case for config entities, such as per-bundle language content settings that not every bundle defines), it would query the persistent cache backend again on every subsequent attempt for that same ID. Now the fact that an ID was not found is also recorded in the per-request static cache, so repeated lookups of the same missing ID skip the cache backend entirely for the rest of the request. Drupal core's performance test suite shows this measurably reduces cache backend reads on real pages: cold-cache node page requests dropped from 225 to 217 cache gets, cold-cache front page requests from 233 to 225, and the administrator node page from 265 to 257 (mostly in the config cache bin), with no change in database query counts.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

In EntityStorageBase::loadMultiple(), after doLoadMultiple() runs, any requested IDs that are still missing are now recorded via a new setNotFoundStaticCache() method, and checked on subsequent calls via getNotFoundFromStaticCache(). Both use a new buildNotFoundCacheId() helper that wraps buildCacheId() with a not_found: prefix, so a storage's own buildCacheId() override (for example ConfigEntityStorage::buildCacheId(), which appends config override keys) is automatically reflected in the not-found cache key too. resetCache() now clears both the entity cache and the not-found cache entries for the given IDs. setStaticCache() was also changed to iterate $entities by its array key (foreach ($entities as $id => $entity)) rather than deriving the cache key from $entity->id(), since the not-found bookkeeping needs to track the originally requested ID.

A new unit test, testLoadMultipleNoResult(), asserts that loading the same nonexistent ID twice in a request results in only a single persistent-cache getMultiple() call. This builds on the earlier bulk-loading work in #3560633 that reduced repeated config entity lookups for per-bundle settings.

item.title: #3614153: Install system module alongside other modules in the installer
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: main
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 44 files, +197/−100 · php +197/−90 · yml +0/−10
  • Diff: 6c4592b

  • Followers: 7

Summary

Drupal's installer previously installed the System module as its own dedicated step before installing anything else, a pattern that dates back to Drupal's early history. This change installs System alongside the other required modules (and, for profiles that declare modules, alongside those too) in the same batch, eliminating an extra service-container rebuild during every installation. As part of removing the special-casing this required, the core "testing" install profile (used by Drupal's own and many contrib functional tests) no longer automatically enables the page_cache and dynamic_page_cache modules. Tests that rely on those modules being present for cache tag or cache header assertions now need to enable them explicitly. Reported savings were significant, one job's test run time dropped from 90 seconds to well under that, and a full functional test job went from over a minute to about two minutes total.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

Previously drupal_install_system() called module_installer->install(['system'], FALSE) directly as an isolated step, and both install_profile_modules() and install_recipe_required_modules() explicitly filtered system out of the module list they installed afterwards (array_diff(array_unique($modules), ['system'])). Now system is simply left in those module lists and installed together with the rest in the normal batch via _install_module_batch(), cutting one container rebuild out of the install path (and, for profiles with declared modules, another).

Because the default language config write (system.site langcode/default_langcode) used to happen right after installing System in drupal_install_system(), that logic moved into _install_module_batch(), which gained a new $install_state parameter (also threaded through install_profile_modules() and install_recipe_required_modules()) so it can still set the language once system shows up in whichever batch group installs it. Since the service container can now be compiled before System module (and its config) exists, DrupalKernel::compileContainer() gained a fallback that reads $GLOBALS['install_state']['parameters']['langcode'] to seed language.default_values when system.site config isn't available yet; this is flagged with a @todo as a temporary workaround pending moving default-language config out of System module entirely (tracked in #3337864).

install_config_import_batch() no longer needs to copy the site UUID from the sync storage into the freshly-created system.site config (the "UUID juggle"), because System module's config is now imported directly rather than being created fresh and then overwritten. Correspondingly, ConfigImporter::validateSiteUuid() now returns TRUE when there's no target system.site config yet, since that indicates a fresh install-from-config rather than a UUID mismatch.

The testing.info.yml/testing_multilingual.info.yml profiles' install: keys for drupal:page_cache and dynamic_page_cache were removed, and many core functional test classes (JSON:API, REST, Views, Block, error/session tests, etc.) were updated to add page_cache and/or dynamic_page_cache to their $modules property, or install them at runtime, wherever the test actually depends on page or dynamic-page caching behavior. This groundwork is what makes #3428372, open for over fifteen years, finally achievable, and several immediate follow-ups were spun off: #3615455 (install database driver modules alongside others), #3614401 (allow install profiles to opt out of being installed), #3614825 (allow additional modules to be installed alongside profile modules), and #3614817 (reduce parallel functional test jobs given the speedup).

Upgrade

If your module's functional tests rely on Drupal core's "testing" install profile having page_cache or dynamic_page_cache enabled by default (for example, to assert cache tags/contexts or X-Drupal-Cache headers), add them explicitly to the test class:

protected static $modules = [
  'your_module',
  'page_cache',
  'dynamic_page_cache',
];

or install them at runtime where needed:

\Drupal::service('module_installer')->install(['page_cache']);

This change is only present on Drupal core's main branch (targeting Drupal 12) and was not backported to 10.x/11.x.

item.description:

Summary

Drupal's asset library system now lets a library declare that it must load before or after another library, in addition to the existing dependencies key. This gives module and theme authors a reliable way to control asset ordering for cases where a real dependency relationship doesn't exist (for example, a library that only reacts to another library if it happens to be present), without resorting to fragile per-file weight values or custom hook_js_alter()/hook_css_alter() code. As part of this change, many long-standing weight overrides and ordering workarounds in core library definitions (jQuery UI assets, contextual, views, settings_tray, CKEditor 5 translations, locale, form_test, and others) were replaced with explicit dependencies, before, or after declarations, or removed outright where dependencies already implied the correct order.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: Asset library definitions in *.libraries.yml now support before and after keys, listing other libraries that must load after or before the declaring library, respectively.

Technical details

The core mechanism for resolving library load order was rewritten around a directed graph instead of ad hoc weight math. LibraryDependencyResolver::doGetDependencies() now builds a graph of libraries and their dependencies as edges, doProcessBeforeAfter() adds extra edges for any before/after keys found in each library's definition (only when the referenced library is already part of the graph), and getLibrariesWithDependencies() runs the result through Drupal\Component\Graph\Graph::searchAndSort() and then sorts by the resulting weight to produce the final load order. getMinimalRepresentativeSubset() was similarly reworked to use the graph's edges rather than repeatedly calling getLibrariesWithDependencies().

AssetResolver::getCssAssets() and getJsAssets() no longer nudge weights by count($css) / 30000 to preserve insertion order; instead they skip re-adding an asset file that has already been added, so the first occurrence (which reflects the correct dependency/before/after order) wins. ckeditor5_js_alter() no longer manipulates a synthetic weight to group translation files for aggregation, it just filters out translation files that don't match the current language via array_filter(). Similarly, locale_js_alter() no longer sets a weight to force the translation file to load first, and settings_tray drops its cssAlter() hook and group: 200 override in favor of an after: [core/drupal.dialog] declaration.

Several core libraries were updated to use before/after: drupal.contextual-links now declares before: [contextual/drupal.context-toolbar], drupal.vertical-tabs gets before: [core/drupal.collapse] (moved from form_test's own weight hack), and test fixture libraries (common_test, js_testing_ajax_request_test) were added to exercise the new keys directly.

item.description:

Summary

Drupal now offers a second, object-oriented way to define database table structures for hook_schema() and similar schema-defining code, alongside the traditional nested associative array. Instead of building a $schema['mytable'] = ['fields' => [...], 'primary key' => [...]] array, module developers can construct a Table object made up of Column, Index, PrimaryKey, UniqueKey, and ForeignKey value objects. These objects validate their own arguments when created (for example, rejecting a length argument on an int column, or a string default on a numeric column), which surfaces schema definition mistakes immediately instead of failing later or silently producing a wrong table. This is purely additive: existing hook_schema() implementations that return arrays keep working exactly as before, nothing needs to change immediately. Core's own conversion of its hook_schema() implementations to the new objects is being done incrementally in follow-up issues.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: New Drupal\Core\Database\SchemaDefinition namespace (Table, Column, Index, PrimaryKey, UniqueKey, ForeignKey, Schema, plus ColumnType/ColumnSize/SchemaDefinitionType enums) and Schema::createSchemaFromDefinition()/createTableFromDefinition() for defining database table structures as an alternative to nested arrays.

Technical details

The new value objects live under Drupal\Core\Database\SchemaDefinition and are immutable and database-abstract: Table holds columns, primaryKey, uniqueKeys, indexes, foreignKeys, and description; Column carries type (ColumnType enum: Char, Varchar, VarcharAscii, Text, Int, Serial, Float, Numeric, Blob), size (ColumnSize enum), and validated modifiers like length, unsigned, precision/scale, binary, serialize. item.title: #3604286: Upsert - Allow to customize the behavior of the update when the insert fails and use more Upsert queries in core
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: main
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 13 files, +283/−32 · php +283/−32
  • Diff: 047e314
  • Discussion: #3604286 · 3 contributors · 34 comments
  • Followers: 5
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 3 contributors

Summary

Drupal's database Upsert query (insert-or-update in one statement) previously always fell back to overwriting a row with the values that were meant to be inserted whenever the insert half of the operation hit an existing key. There was no way to say "update this column based on its current value" (for example, incrementing a counter atomically). This change extends Upsert so a per-column update expression can be supplied, and several core subsystems that previously used the older, less efficient Merge query (which does a separate select plus insert/update) were converted to use it: cache tag invalidation counters, file usage counts, and the search index word score. As a bonus, cache tag invalidations, and the other converted operations, now happen in a single atomic database round trip instead of two.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: New Drupal\Core\Database\Expression value object and Drupal\Core\Database\Query\UpsertUpdateExpression subclass let an Upsert query run a column specific SQL expression (e.g. incrementing a counter) instead of overwriting the column with the insert value when a row already exists.

Technical details

The core addition is Drupal\Core\Database\Expression, a simple value object holding an expression string plus keyed arguments, and Drupal\Core\Database\Query\UpsertUpdateExpression, a thin subclass of it used specifically for upsert update overrides. Upsert::fields() was extended so entries can mix plain column names (for the insert list) with column => new UpsertUpdateExpression(...) pairs; the latter are collected into a new $updateExpressions property and their arguments are merged into the bound query parameters in execute(). If fields() receives an associative array mixing plain insert values with an UpsertUpdateExpression, or an expression entry without a string column key, it throws \InvalidArgumentException.

Each driver's Upsert::__toString() (mysql's ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE, pgsql's and sqlite's ON CONFLICT ... DO UPDATE) now substitutes the raw expression for a column instead of VALUES($field) / EXCLUDED.$field when one was supplied. The mysql driver's execute() binds expression arguments with bindValue() rather than bindParam(), since by-reference binding inside a loop would make every placeholder share the same final loop variable.

Using this, Drupal\Core\Cache\CacheTagsChecksum::doInvalidateTags(), Drupal\file\FileUsage\DatabaseFileUsageBackend::add(), and search_index word scoring in search.module were converted from merge()/expression() to upsert() with an UpsertUpdateExpression for the incrementing column. Conversions of Drupal\Core\KeyValueStore\DatabaseStorage, StringDatabaseStorage, and TaxonomyHooks were explicitly left out of scope, per discussion in the issue, and remain on Merge. hook_entity_predelete() and hook_ENTITY_TYPE_predelete() example code in core/lib/Drupal/Core/Entity/entity.api.php was updated to demonstrate the Upsert equivalent of the old Merge pattern.

Upgrade

Custom code using Merge purely to emulate an atomic counter or expression based update can switch to Upsert with an UpsertUpdateExpression, for example:

$connection->upsert('example_deleted_entity_statistics')
  ->key(['type', 'id'])
  ->fields([
    'type',
    'id',
    'count' => new UpsertUpdateExpression('{example_deleted_entity_statistics}.[count] + :count', [':count' => $count]),
  ])
  ->values([
    'type' => $type,
    'id' => $id,
    'count' => $count,
  ])
  ->execute();

This is not a breaking change: Upsert::fields() remains backward compatible for plain column/value usage.

item.title: #3565258: Support library-specific aggregates
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Major task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 27 files, +624/−116 · php +573/−102 · yml +51/−14
  • Diff: d9cc509

  • Followers: 23
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 9 contributors

Summary

Drupal's asset library system can now mark specific CSS or JavaScript libraries so their files are always bundled into their own aggregate, regardless of which other libraries happen to be attached on a given page. Previously, the exact set of libraries in an aggregate, and therefore its URL and query string, varied depending on everything else loaded on that particular page, so browsers and CDNs often re-downloaded effectively the same CSS or JS just because the query string differed slightly from page to page. By setting the new aggregate_target key on a library, its aggregate gets a predictable, page-independent URL, which increases browser and CDN cache hit rates for repeat and multi-page visits. Core has already applied this to several always-loaded libraries (core/drupal, core/drupalSettings, system/base, parts of Umami and Claro) and switched some small vendor JS libraries to preprocess: false instead, since aggregating a single already-minified file offers no benefit.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: AssetResolverInterface::getCssAssets() and ::getJsAssets() gained an optional $with_dependencies parameter (default TRUE); custom implementations of the interface must add it to stay compatible.
  • New API: New aggregate_target library definition key (with css and js sub-keys, each accepting true or an arbitrary string) forces a library's assets into a dedicated, page-independent aggregate.

Technical details

Library definitions can now declare aggregate_target: {css: ..., js: ...}, where the value is either true (unique per library) or an arbitrary string shared by several libraries meant to be co-located. LibraryDiscoveryParser::buildByExtension() normalizes this to ['css' => FALSE, 'js' => FALSE] when absent, and also records each CSS file's SMACSS category so it can be checked later. CssCollectionGrouper::group() and JsCollectionGrouper::group() track, per group, whether all files belonging to a targeted library (and, for CSS, a given category) landed contiguously in a single group via a $first_seen_libraries/$seen_index mechanism; if a library's files get split across groups because of per-file weights or other libraries interleaving, the libraries key is dropped from those groups and the aggregate silently falls back to the pre-existing include/exclude/delta behavior.

When a group does carry a libraries key, CssCollectionOptimizerLazy::optimize() and JsCollectionOptimizerLazy::optimize() build the asset URL using a compressed libraries query argument (and, for CSS, a category argument, since a single library can still span multiple categories) instead of include/exclude/delta. CssAssetsController/JsAssetsController::deliver() and their shared AssetControllerBase were updated to accept these new parameters and, when present, call AssetResolverInterface::getCssAssets()/getJsAssets() with the new $with_dependencies = FALSE argument so the aggregate is rebuilt from exactly the listed libraries rather than pulling in their full dependency trees.

Core's core.libraries.yml, system.libraries.yml, big_pipe.libraries.yml, Umami's and Claro's .libraries.yml files were updated to use aggregate_target on libraries that are effectively always loaded together (e.g. core/drupal and core/drupalSettings share js: 'drupal'; loadjs, drupal.htmx, and htmx share js: 'htmx'). Umami's global library was split into global and a new global_tweaks dependency to isolate files whose custom weights would otherwise have prevented the aggregate target from applying.

Upgrade

To opt a library into a dedicated aggregate, add aggregate_target to its definition in a *.libraries.yml file:

mylibrary:
  aggregate_target:
    css: true
    js: 'mygroup'
  css:
    theme:
      css/mylibrary.css: {}
  js:
    js/mylibrary.js: {}

Use true for a library-specific aggregate, or an arbitrary string shared across libraries that are always expected to load together. This only takes effect if all of the library's files end up contiguous within a single asset group; libraries that set custom per-file weights, or that get split apart by other libraries' weights, transparently fall back to the previous aggregation behavior.

Code that implements AssetResolverInterface directly (rather than extending AssetResolver) needs to add the new bool $with_dependencies = TRUE parameter to getCssAssets() and getJsAssets() to remain compatible with the interface.

item.title: #3524971: Defend against \GuzzleHttp\Cookie\FileCookieJar gadget chain
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 4 files, +304/−3 · php +299 · lock +3/−2 · json +2/−1

  • Followers: 9

Summary

Drupal 11.x now ships a hardened replacement for Guzzle's \GuzzleHttp\Cookie\FileCookieJar class, closing off a publicly known "gadget chain" that can be abused to write an arbitrary file to the server. On its own this class isn't reachable by an attacker, it only becomes dangerous if a site (core or, more likely, a contrib or custom module) also has a PHP Object Injection vulnerability that lets attacker-controlled data reach unserialize(). With this fix in place, even if such a vulnerability existed elsewhere, this particular gadget chain would no longer be usable to write files. This is defense in depth, not a fix for a standalone vulnerability, and requires no action from site owners beyond updating.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Security: Backports Guzzle 8.0's hardening of \GuzzleHttp\Cookie\FileCookieJar (a private autoSave flag disabled by __wakeup()) into an early-loaded shim, closing a PHP Object Injection-chained arbitrary file write gadget on Drupal 11.x. Not independently exploitable; requires a separate deserialization vulnerability.

Technical details

The underlying issue is in Guzzle itself: FileCookieJar::__destruct() calls save(), which writes $this->filename to disk. If an attacker can get arbitrary serialized data into unserialize() (via some other PHP Object Injection bug), they can craft a FileCookieJar instance with an attacker-chosen $filename and cookie payload; when PHP garbage-collects it, __destruct() writes that payload to the attacker's chosen path, a classic deserialization file-write gadget (documented in PHPGGC's Guzzle/FW/1 chain). Guzzle's maintainers eventually landed a fix for Guzzle 8.0 (https://github.com/guzzle/guzzle/pull/3334) adding a private $autoSave flag that __wakeup() sets to false and __destruct() checks before saving, so an unserialized instance never persists to disk. Drupal core was still on Guzzle 7.x, which lacks this hardening.

Rather than removing or aliasing the class (approaches discussed earlier in the issue, including using the core.moved_classes mechanism from #3502882), the committed fix backports the Guzzle 8.0 hardened implementation verbatim into a new core/includes/guzzle_file_cookie_jar_shim.php, registered in composer.json's autoload.files list alongside bootstrap.inc. Composer's files autoload entries are required unconditionally and very early, before PSR-4 autoloading for anything else kicks in, so this shim's class GuzzleHttp\Cookie\FileCookieJar (guarded by a class_exists(..., false) check) gets declared first and pre-empts the classloader from ever loading Guzzle's own, unhardened copy of the file. The shim preserves full functionality, normal instantiation still auto-saves on __destruct(), but any instance produced via unserialize() has autoSave forced to false by __wakeup(), so the file-write gadget is inert. This is a temporary measure: the @todo in the shim notes it should be removed once Drupal updates to Guzzle 8, which already happened on the main branch in #3612544; this fix was committed only to the 11.x branch since it will still be supported for some time and the composer.json changes did not backport cleanly to older branches.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: May 16, 2025
  • Committed: August 4, 2026 (1 year later)

Key contributors

  • catch (Third and Grove)
  • nod_ (Très Bien Tech)
  • cmlara (DM13 Security LLC)

The approach evolved considerably over the issue's life. mcdruid initially explored removing the class from the autoloader or aliasing it via the core.moved_classes mechanism from #3502882, but found in testing that if the original vendor file was still present on disk, PHP would still autoload the real class instead of the alias, undermining that approach. cmlara pushed back on the earlier "just remove it" direction, pointing out that auditing only Drupal-namespace contrib code for usage risks false negatives since the class could be used anywhere in a site's full dependency stack, and that removing the class without a replacement risked white-screen-of-death failures for sites that do legitimately use it. This feedback steered the fix away from removal and toward the front-running shim approach that longwave suggested (citing the precedent in #3224421), which preserves the class's full API while neutralizing the gadget.
